title: close --summary names each goal clause of the sprint and the item that carried it
goal: backlog.py close --summary prints the sprint's goal split into its clauses (by '; ' and ', and'), each with the done item whose goal covers it or 'unmet' and the item that now carries it, so a clause whose item was deferred mid-sprint shows at the close; a test plants a sprint whose clause item was moved out. Answers the SP-w3xmbdra retrospective: goal clause 1 (seed pack index) went unmet when ST-4mcoplex was deferred, and only the review notes said so.

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_land
class B:
    items = {
        'SP-1': {'kind': 'sprint', 'goal': "story b exists and is written; the bug's file c exists, and the release notes carry every flag"},
        'ST-1': {'kind': 'story', 'status': 'done', 'title': 'Story', 'goal': 'story b exists and is written'},
        'BG-1': {'kind': 'bug', 'status': 'done', 'title': 'Bug', 'goal': "the bug's file c exists"},
        'ST-9': {'kind': 'story', 'status': 'open', 'title': 'Release notes', 'goal': 'the release notes carry every flag'},
    }
    def label(self, i):
        return i + ' [' + self.items[i]['title'] + ']'
out = bl_land.goal_clause_lines(B(), 'SP-1', ['ST-1', 'BG-1'])
want = ['goal clauses:',
    '  1. story b exists and is written: ST-1 [Story]',
    "  2. the bug's file c exists: BG-1 [Bug]",
    '  3. the release notes carry every flag: unmet, carried by ST-9 [Release notes]']
assert out == want, out
